review_text_clean: we hired a jeep and driver from habanera, their company name was special safari, the driver was giayan kaluarachchi and their number is 0763101482. they are situated in habanera, near cinnamon lodge. we looked on here and took advice to not book in advance, but to go to habanara and hire a local guide and keep. this was excellent advice. hire special safari as they were fantastic! i read that older jeeps are better as they can go through the water in the park and not get stuck - this was true. we sailed through whilst other newer jeeps became stuck. our driver was an excellent guide, he knew exactly where to go to see a multitude of animals. we saw elephants, mongoose, snake, jackals, eagles, deer, herds of water buffaloes, monkeys, peacocks, herons, bee eater, monitor lizards to name but a few. our driver giayan was patient, there was never a rush. we set off at at 2.10pm and returned at 6.30pm, giving us 3.5 hours in the park its about 30 mins from special safari in the middle of habanara to the middle of the park. we were one of the last jeeps to leave the park as we were having such a great time and our guide was so busy showing us all the animals we could think of! i cant recommend special safari highly enough to do the safari in minneriya. the other thing to note is that the elephants move between parks, so hiring locally meant that giayan knew exactly where the elephants were and took us straight to them.

review_text_clean: yes there are a lot of jeeps, but i felt this park was more open and avoided a lot of the crush i felt with yala national park the highlight being to try and spot an elusive sri lankan leopard or sloth bear. the jeeps on this occasion had room to manoeuvre and the elephants were all very obliging and all jeeps kept their distance and even waited if elephants approached to let them have their way. so i did enjoy this park much more - seeing elephant families doing their own thing without being hassled by the jeeps was most enjoyable. birdlife was the only other wildlife but there were large and small herds everywhere in this park and i didnt feel the jostling of jeeps too much. most drove up slowly, found a position and parked to allow us to take photographs or just enjoy their antics. on our safari i didnt feel that the jeep drivers were encroaching on the elephants as all the jeeps seem to follow the track, parked off to the side and allowed us to just watch the elephants - yes mothers put their babies on the other side of the jeeps, but continued feeding, and the babies of course continued playing. i actually quite enjoyed the afternoon safari as instead of getting hotter, it cooled as the afternoon sun began to set. we were a private group with our own guide so we had a pre-arranged driver for this attraction, so it was just us in a slightly newer and more comfortable jeep - open topped and a little dusty, but allowed you to stand and take photos when the jeep stopped. have an open mind here - sri lankan is a developing country and has a long way to go so dont expect the same level of eco-tourism you would get in other countries.

review_text_clean: this is the perfect drive in the evening, even though we didnt have any plan of visiting this park, our guide suggested to do this, so we went ahead and we were not disappointed. its an 2-3 hour long safari in the park and they take you near the lake where elephants come there to eat. its the perfect time to visit as you would end up seeing so many so close. i think they are used to so many jeeps coming close everyday so they were busy eating and we were ignored most of the time by them. so we closely watched how they eat the grass, the way they pull out, dust it out and then eat. it was an amazing experience to watch them so close. we were taken another side of the lake for a nice view which you can climb few stairs to watch and if you are keen just to get the legs dirty after. the surprising visitors were variety of birds, they were awesome. i wish i had more time to spot them more.

review_text_clean: if you are looking for an exclusive observation of elephants grazing in herds by the lake edge you are going to be disappointed. this is a popular tourist attraction and the convoy of vehicles winding their way along the dirt roads to find elephants is at times intrusive. having said that you are likely to have the opportunity to see groups of elephants as we did. there were many with young, one or two month old babies and they genuinely seemed unconcerned with the vehicles nearby. for the most part drivers showed some respect for the elephants welfare and maintained a good distance. in many instances the elephants ambled slowly closer to the vehicles. if you decide to go my suggestion would be to go late afternoon, say from 3.00pm onwards. this way you escape the heat of the day. there are dozens of drivers outside the park entrance ready to take you.
aspect_sentences: ['this way you escape the heat of the day.']

review_text_clean: this was our first of 3 safari experiences in sri lanka. the jeep was in average condition, 3 rows of seats, with open roofs where you could stand up. all the jeeps follow the same track, up to 2 abreast at a time. you go through bush, then through a river 3 jeeps got stuck - fortunately not ours and then it opens out to large areas surrounding the lake. we saw a couple of hundred elephants best to go on an afternoon safari as they come to the lake for water. unfortunately there were almost as many jeeps as elephants and at first we sat in a huge queue the jeeps at the front of the line didnt move on in a timely manner. after a while the jeeps spread out and there were plenty more elephants to see, with less crowded jeep conditions. our driver didnt really talk to us, but it was pretty obvious what we were looking at! if youre into elephants this is the safari for you.
aspect_sentences: ['the jeep was in average condition, 3 rows of seats, with open roofs where you could stand up.']

review_text_clean: sadly this wildlife park is being over-exploited, with convoys of jeeps in search of a limited number of elephants. when a herd was spotted, the dirt track turned into a 4x4 sales forecourt, with jeeps jostling for space and the best view. we also saw a few larger birds egrets, eagles, herons and pelicans, and a mongoose. ironically, we saw two elephants one of them with tasks, quite rare by the side of the road on our drive back to the hotel. our driver was quick to spot them in the semi-darkness, and we were much closer to them than in the wildlife park. our expectations may have been too high, as we had already visited yala national park earlier in our holiday. i would give minneriya a miss and spend the extra time at yala. a more diverse range of animals and birds, with less jeeps!!
aspect_sentences: ['our driver was quick to spot them in the semi-darkness, and we were much closer to them than in the wildlife park.']

review_text_clean: the ecco park is supposedly a sanctuary for wild elephants but it has now become completely over-commercialized by greedy tours firms all congesting parts of the park in their diesel polluting vehicles. we were on an organised trip that lasted several hours much of which was spent in traffic jams of vehicles all travelling along the same track but often several lines abreast and in different directions as individual drivers each sought to outdo the numerous other vehicles. some broke down or attempted ridiculous three-point turns in the track only to become stuck in the mud thus causing various blockages. at one point we didnt move for nearly an hour. imagine a crowded street full of tuck tuks all vying to get to the same spot and not caring about the chaos created and the effect on the elephants. most importantly the elephants space isnt respected so they were sometimes chased by selfish drivers. it was an appalling experience for the animals and the far too numerous visitors alll congested into very tight areas. website photos suggest large open spaces and numerous elephants enjoying the peaceful sanctuary but instead we saw a mere handful and on each occasion they were quickly approached from various directions by numerous jeeps. its just become a commercial rip off for greedy firms. overall it was chaotic, disrespectful of the elephants and an appalling excursion. avoid!!!!
aspect_sentences: ['imagine a crowded street full of tuck tuks all vying to get to the same spot and not caring about the chaos created and the effect on the elephants.']

review_text_clean: it is the largest concentration and gathering of asian elephants that can be seen anywhere in the world. we did an open top jeep safari, watching baby elephants playing with each other, bull elephants tussling for dominance and the great matriarchs surveying the scene is not a sight you are likely to forget in a hurry. inside the park you will also come across some wild boar, peacocks, deer and many more animals roaming freely as nature intended them to live. aside from the elephant, minneriya is also home to some 23 other species of mammals a paradise for many species of lizard and you will see them here in all their colour if you look carefully enough. the views are stunning. youll see hundreds of birds, storks, pheasants, beer eaters, herons, pelicans, eagles, etc. there are also spotted deers roaming around. the driver was knowledgeable and would point at different species. as well as snakes like the indian python and the mugger crocodile. above all, of course, are sri lankas wonderfully varied bird population. we drove for over an hour seeing birds, butterflies, tortoises, deers and when we thought viewings were over, we saw a young grey leopard. it was just breath-taking. then more stunning scenery and you will also encounter deer, buffalo, pelicans and peacocks. despite the heat it was a great afternoon at the park. the drivers are constantly in contact with each other and updating where the elephants are to be seen. i highly recommend this to everyone.

review_text_clean: went on a jeep safari as part of our sri lanka tour. wonderful to see so many asian elephants but it felt like the drivers were chasing down the elephants! there was nearly as many jeeps as elephants and it didnt seem much consideration was given to the wildlife, elephants especially. we have been on safari in africa where there is a 2 vehicle limit to protect the animals from over exposure, this was certainly not the case here. concerned how much of the money raised from the safari actually goes to the protection and conservation of these endangered animals, i believe it probably goes to purchasing more jeeps!! would not give them my money again until i was convinced a large percentage was being used for conservation purposes. their tactics and approach should be monitored by animal welfare groups to ensure it is in the animals interests.

review_text_clean: we knew that the herd flitted between minneriya and kaudulla but heard there where elephants at the former. there are literally hundreds of operators out of habarana and i think most hotels guest houses either run or know someone who does. we went with our stay sagiriya water gardens and the guy was excellent, we even saw a single elephant on the way to the park. once at the entrance you have to pay for each individual in the jeep and there is a discount for jeeps with more people in so a couple will pay slightly more than a jeep with four and so on. once in the park it takes a while to reach the lake but we saw multiple elephants on the way, then two herds of about 30 elephants at the lake ranging in age and size from cute little ones to one of the largest who was only one of two with tusks. what an incredible day, and our guide held right back and kept a good distance, where we saw others too close.

review_text_clean: minneriya is reputed to be the home of the largest herd of asian elephants, and our experience in april 2017 would seem to bear that out. despite the commercialisation of the trip - there must have been 50 land cruisers around the reservoir - the park is big enough to give one a good view of the herd, especially as it gathers in late afternoon before going into the forest to sleep. they came from all around, to drink, wash and play in the shallow waters, before setting off in a column and heading back into the forest - and they were so quiet. no squealing from the baby elephants, nor thudding of feet from the adults, but simply an inexorable susuration as they walked past us. the area is also home to many other species, and we saw many types of bird, including the omni-present egrets, ibis and other water fowl. there are also crocodiles, and we saw a couple basking on the banks. a great experience.
aspect_sentences: ['a great experience.']

review_text_clean: did a safri here and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. we travelled in open top jeep so you could stand up and really take in the sights. big open areas and lakes where the elephants go to play and drink in the water. the elephants wander around ignoring all the jeeps so seems quite natural instead of seeing them in a captive situation. before we went there, i just thought we would see a few elephants and it would be no big deal but i was wrong. we seen about 150 and quite a few calves as well. one of the high lights of our sl holiday. saw lots of birdlife as well .

review_text_clean: well worth a visit. we visited both udawalawe and minneriya and if youre only able to do one then 100 do udawalawe as its way less tourist crowded and you get more up close to the elephants without actually disturbing them. at minneriya we were lucky enough to see loads of elephants, probably 100 in total but there was easily 100 jeeps all vying for the best view and its gets really chaotic. the elephants just want to get to the water and with the jeeps all in a line they almost block the elephants which doesnt seem very animal-centric. we didnt pressure our driver but you could see other tourists pushing their driver to get in front of others for a better photo. dont get me wrong, a beautiful place and the elephants are magnificent.

review_text_clean: a must do on our agenda! piled into the back of jeeps 5 seats headed into the national park on a fine day with the roof open no side wall giving great views. the driver was great driving along spotting various animals in the bush and grass. the highlight took a little time with us seeing various monkeys, birds water buffalo before finding the elephants a couple of large herds. the elephants were amazing - probably 50 to 80 in total they were so carefree despite our close attendance. at the busiest time there must have been 50 jeeps 4wds parked up with cameras clicking amongst many excited people. the elephants mainly ate grass however a few entered the lake. we also ascended a small tower for better views over the countryside lake - be careful as no handrails. nothing special but part of the tour. took a bit of a drive back to the buscar park where we met numerous monkeys a couple of relatively tame deer. great fun even for the older less mobile folk in our group.

review_text_clean: dont go to other sanctuaries, visit minneriya if you want to see elephants in their natural environment, thriving, playing and reproducing in a healthy setting. we did a 3 hour safari. theres not a huge amount to see apart from elephants, but there are lots of then and you can get close to them closest was about 10 metres from the jeep. the safari is basic but fun, you park in the car park, climb in the back of a jeep and get driven around the park to seek out the elephants. we went in the afternoon as thats when they are most likely to congregate at the lake. our jeep driver was very good, the two of us bounced around in the back - just two side benches, three padded cross bars to hold onto if you want to stand up. no health safety here - hold on tight to avoid bashing your bits against the side of the jeep, and if standing, duck to avoid branches thwacking you in the face! remember sun cream as theres no cover, and a hat is risky to blow off if theres wind. we saw loads of elephants - noisy, playful, muddy, but and small. there was one suckling its mother, still a bit pink, that our driver said was about ten days old. we did this as part of a four day tour which originally had the elephant sanctuary in its itinerary, but switched to minneriya before we travelled. we are so pleased, as people concerned with animal welfare, opposed to elephant tricks and rides and tethering, but still wanting to be close to the magnificent beasts.

review_text_clean: it was great to see such large numbers of elephants in the family groups - matriarch, babies, youngsters, teenagers. then with the young males who had been kicked out from the herd just feeding a short way from the main herd. interesting to watch the antics of some larger males finding their way into the smaller herds to check out the females. yes there are a lot of safari jeeps but it did not seem as chaotic as in the yala national park and i think this is due to the fact that this park has a rather large open area of grass around lakes that allow for the army of jeeps to park by the road and allow for viewing by everyone as there were elephants everywhere. in yala once an elusive leopard is found, its a race on for ever driver to get their clients a sighting and the tracks are narrow and not as open as in minneriya. i loved watching the babies, and yes the protective mothers keeping their bodies to the jeep side, but both continued grazing whilst we looked on. watching elephant behaviour was interesting - a mother comin out from a bamboo thicket as we approached in the jeep. we stopped. she stopped. she waited - we didnt move. then obviously when she thought it was safe, she signalled to the two younger elephants and one by one out of the thicket they came and crossed the track. i didnt feel the driver of our safari jeep hassled the elephants at all. all the jeeps seemed to give them the space. if the elephant came behind the jeep, the driver stopped, waited for the elephant to pass or do what it wanted, before the driver proceeded along the track the park appears to have designated trails that the vehicles can use and the jeeps generally stated on this track or to the side if they needed to pass. its main purpose for this park i think is for wild elephant viewing, but we also saw lots of birdlife around the lake. we did an afternoon safari from 3pm and i found the seats were very nicely padded in our vehicle but seatbelts i think are optional, but then i was standing up a lot when the vehicle was parked or moving slowly along. its not for everyone as its hot, its bumpy, but i enjoyed it.

review_text_clean: this is one of three safaris we did in sri lanka, and was by far the least enjoyable. it seems that there is little regard for the environment or the wildlife as a large number of vehicles thrash around a relatively small area. i had the feeling that the tour was not about the wildlife at all, but about giving tourists a four wheel drive experience - not what we signed up for. the park itself appears to be in a sad state with many invasive weed species the roads are overused by the heavy vehicle traffic and poorly maintained. we saw a few elephants, but the experience was marred by the volume of jeeps jostling for position. we got much more enjoyment out of seeing wild elephants by the side of the road than we did on this tour - save your money.
aspect_sentences: ['the park itself appears to be in a sad state with many invasive weed species the roads are overused by the heavy vehicle traffic and poorly maintained.']

review_text_clean: the whole experience is very staged and disappointing. the problem is that the vegetation is very high and dense in the park, so while you do see elephants and other animals, they are usually far in the distance and you can only see them through lenses or binoculars. also the variety of what we saw was very limited. after about 2 hours, all of the jeeps then take you to a large look out point high on a hill. while it was beautiful, again you can only see animals far in the distance unless you get lucky. it all seemed very stage like a disney-world, andino in the final scene. dont waste your money! we later went to udawalawe national park in the south and it was spectacular. we saw numerous animals and birds very close up. it also cost us far less...30 per person compared to 50 in minneriya.

review_text_clean: although we hired a private jeep it wasnt quite the intimate experience you imagine. transfer to the park from the hotel was swift, im fairly certain our driver was trained by lewis hamilton. entry to the park is chaotic with the car park heaving with other vehicles waiting to get in followed by a long wait to start moving along a dusty track bumper to bumper. i never imagined eyes watering with dust exhaust fumes that you would see anything but our expert tracker seemed to know that if there were 30 or so jeeps huddled together there might be something worth seeing. once you see the elephants and there are plenty including some only weeks old, all you can do is focus on them. they switch off the engines and you can watch at close range as they go about eating with their young rolling in the mud.we even saw some tuskers that the guide said are quite rare. it was a good afternoon although they probably allow too many vehicles in i wanted to go as much as the next person enjoyed being so close to the elephants.

review_text_clean: we were staying at habarana and its a 15 min drive to the entrance of the national park. the ticket price calculation is a bit weird as all price lists are displayed in the local language only . three of us in a jeep cost me sl rupees 9840 as entrance fees for us and jeep driver plus slr 5000 for the jeep rental . wish the prices were better explained in english as is done at other places. we were lucky to have the services of kavinda thushan who ensured that we moved in at the appropriate time ie 3pm and saw atleast 3 large groups of wild elephants , including a solo rogue tusker. all in all we would have seen 70-80 elephants. it is a bit tricky as there is another national park , across the road name starting with k . elephants keep on moving and there are times when sighting wud be nil in minneriya as all elephant herds would have moved across the road to the other park. we spent time till 530 pm in the park and saw elephants of all sizes from very small babies to large tuskers. water buffaloes also inhabit this park and so do peacocks , monkeys and other animals. there is a huge lake inside the park called habarana lake which attracts all wild animals. definitely worth a visit. take your camera and binocs as they would be handy.
aspect_sentences: ['the ticket price calculation is a bit weird as all price lists are displayed in the local language only .', 'wish the prices were better explained in english as is done at other places.']

review_text_clean: if you intend to see a lot of elephants enjoying in their natural habitat, eating, drinking and having fun, this is the place for you. our driver had a contact for the jeep safari and thus we didnt book in advance. the park is vast, full of greenery and spread across nearly 9000 hectares. as it was a weekday, there were not much people, just a few jeeps doing the safari. the site of more than 60-70 elephants at one place, enjoying their time, was really beautiful and satisfying. plenty of playful baby elephants seen!! there are a lot of bird species as well in the park. our safari driver was sharp-eyed and knowledgeable, spotting and identifying birds at a distance and stopping to let us take photos. the safari took nearly 2.5 hours to complete. all in all, it was worth the price paid for!!

review_text_clean: there are monkeys, various species of birds and water buffalo a plenty to get you excited but we were very fortunate to see two different elephant herds at close range. the first was a reasonably large herd which were by the waters edge. this herd had many adult elephants and three young tuskers. the second herd crossed the road directly, and very close to, the rear of our stationary jeep. they were almost in touching distance, amazing animals to get so close to. again we were lucky enough to see yet another mid aged tusker. it is advisable to cover yourself up well and to use plenty of sun cream as the jeep is open top and the sun is unrelenting. a must do activity for anyone lucky enough to get the opportunity to do so.

review_text_clean: weve been on one safari in india to see tigers and have left dismayed and poorer because it of course is down to luck and on on both occasions saw nothing more than a bird or monkey. so the thought of doing a safari to possibly see elephants was not top of our list in sri lanka. but our driver said we wouldnt be disappointed so we gave it a go. first impressions great - we had our own jerk and driver. none of the group squeezing into one huge jeep for twenty with limited views. as we entered the national park and drove around for 15mins i started to recognise in myself that desperation you feel looking for anything, something to make you think you just might see an animal. after another five minutes we slowed down and poking its head through some palms was a huge elephant munching on some food. that alone left us happy and content as it had already surpassed expectations. amazing we then drove around the corner and found ourselves surrounded - literally surrounded by a herd of about 300 elephants. all slowly eating and gradually edging toward a lake for water. we saw families, babies and even rare tusked elephants apparently only about 6 have tusks here. words cannot describe the experience. we slowly drive around with them for an hour finding it hard to pull ourselves away. we eventually did to drive around another corner of the lake only to have another herd of about 200 doing the same. there is nothing more amazing than watching the sunset and these amazing animals calmly go about their business with no fear of humans or the jeep and most importantly in their natural habitat living wild. make sure you do this. it was an experience of a lifetime and the highlight of two weeks in sri lanka

review_text_clean: our driver chathu from sri lanka wide tours arranged this at short notice with his friend amila, a jeep driver at the park. the 2 of them really made this a great experience but you really have to get over the sheer volume of other jeeps at the waters edge where all the elephants congregate to get the most out of this. there were alot of elephants to see including a family with a week old baby. you could watch them all for hours and its a great setting with the lake as a backdrop. amila managed to get us off the beaten track and away from the masses for most of the trip where we were able to see a variety of birds, monkeys, lizards and deer. there were no bears or leopards to be seen but elephants are what you come to see here for the most part. we came across a wounded elephant alone in the bush on the way back. apparently the park was aware of it but inter-departmental politics and red tape was preventing something being done about it. the elephant was clearly in pain. chathu and amila both called the ministers office in colombo while we were there and ended up getting something done about it. the calls were flying back and forward to amila. we were very impressed by his tenacity in trying to get something done about it.

review_text_clean: this park is just off the main road from habarana to polynaruwa. we took a jeep safari ............. which means you stand up in the back of a jeep, holding on to the roll bars. nothing much to see as you enter down a dusty track - but then it opens out to a flat area by the lake, where there are a lot of elephants ..................and a lot of jeeps! some of the jeep drivers could do with better training, as they get too close and spook the animals - but its still goo and there are plenty of birds to see by the lake. not really a safari, but quite an interesting drive around for around 2-3 hours. the good news is that they only allow the jeeps in between 6am and 6pm - no night time drives .................but there are a lot of jeeps. they need to be careful or theyll spoil this by unregulated commercialism.
aspect_sentences: ['they need to be careful or theyll spoil this by unregulated commercialism.']

review_text_clean: we were staying in habarana and had pre-booked a safari in this national park with walkers tours. in short, this was a fabulous experience. the jeep picked us up at the hotel then took us about 20 mins down the road to the park. after a short delay where the driver bought the tickets, he drove us into the park. pretty much immediately we saw spotted deer then we drove through the jungle for about 20 minutes down to minnerya tank and saw roughly 80 elephants in abou 10 different groups or some were alone. we also saw a huge variety of birds. our walkers tours guide was hugely knowledgable about the bird names, elephant ages etc. we never expected to see so many elephants in a 2.5 hour trip. brilliant!!

review_text_clean: minneriya national park is on the way to polonruwa, just around 10 kms from habarana town. you have lot of options from jeep drivers and hotels, guest house who can organize the safari into the national park. its best to visit the park in the afternoon at 3 pm as you have better chance of sighting elephants other animals, birds in the park. the jeep safari should not cost more than lkr srilankan rupees 3500-4000 for the entire jeep. the entrance tickets to the park is steep but worth the price. the jeep can seat easily 6 persons. check out the jeep before you agree on confirming the same. go for jeep which is more open type with good space to stand and view the wildlife. some jeeps have 2-3 rows of seats which makes the jeep cramped and no space to stand for viewing animals. the park has dense population of elephants. you are sure to sight elephants at close proximity specially near the lake within the park. apart from elephants there are quite a few birds you can sight near the lake and water bodies within the park. the safari is for 2 hours and almost all the jeep drivers are knowledgeable about the route within the park and places to sight elephants. the jeep safari has a pit stop at lake where you can get down and take pictures. there is tower near the pit stop to get views of lake and park. overall a must visit place if you are staying in habarana or near by place.
aspect_sentences: ['the entrance tickets to the park is steep but worth the price.', 'the jeep can seat easily 6 persons.', 'some jeeps have 2-3 rows of seats which makes the jeep cramped and no space to stand for viewing animals.']

review_text_clean: while visiting sirigiya, we decided to visit minneriya national park and it was the best decision we could make. i have seen but reviews of people saying it was crowded. it must have been we went late during the day, but we just came across 2 more jeeps in the whole safari we arrived just after 3pm. we were travelling with locals who arranged a safari driver that was at the entrance for only rs3000 bear in mind that you may be overcharged if you dont have someone to negotiate it. the entrance fee is almost none for locals and quite higher for foreigners, but still quite reasonable. we started the safari and were able stand up on the jeep and get amazing views. the first part of the route is a dense forest, but when you reach the opening, the views are stunning. youll see hundreds of birds, storks, pheasants, beer eaters, herons, pelicans, eagles, etc. there are also spotted deers roaming around. the driver was knowledgeable and would point at different species. we saw elephants far away, then, a lonely one 50 meters away and then we came close to three, i.e. a mum with the two kids. we were totally amazed at seeing wild animals at less than 30 meters away and suddenly the protective and caring mother charged at us. it was terrifying yet astounding. the mum just wanted to ensure that we didnt hurt her kids. we drove for over an hour seeing birds, butterflies, tortoises, deers and when we thought viewings were over we saw a young grey leopard. it was just breathtaking, but the young fellow disappeared before we got our cameras out so it only got imprinted in our memories. overall, we spent 2 hours enjoying beautiful views and spotting some of sri lankan amazing wild life. highly recommended.
aspect_sentences: ['youll see hundreds of birds, storks, pheasants, beer eaters, herons, pelicans, eagles, etc.', 'it was just breathtaking, but the young fellow disappeared before we got our cameras out so it only got imprinted in our memories.']

review_text_clean: i am not an elephant person. never have been. i would see an elephant or two at the zoo and be ..... meh. but minneriya ... rocked. my. world. it starts with a 30 minute ride in a jeep from the entrance into the heart of the national park. the roads are good, you can stand up in the back of the jeep and you are racing through the jungle with the wind in your hair exhilarating! and we hadnt seen our first elephant yet! during the next three hours, we encountered lone male elephants who challenged our small jeep for dominance, a young mum with babies in tow who was determined to chase us away to protect her babies and then a herd by the lake. the herd must have been close to 200 elephants the sight was mesmerising. groups of elephants bathing, males warily standing apart watching the jeeps and each other, baby elephants running excitedly from group to group tooting their little trunks. it was the most gorgeous experience. and it is not just elephants, we also saw flocks of birds, a herd of water buffalo and one crocodile sub-bathing. a brilliant afternoon, we loved this experience so much that we almost considered going back a second time!
aspect_sentences: ['the herd must have been close to 200 elephants the sight was mesmerising.']

review_text_clean: my wife and i just did a safari here and it was pretty amazing! we had a great driver that our guest house booked for us mansala safari resort, which i highly recommend. the view from the small private jeeps cant be beat! youre mostly going to see lots of elephants and some very close up. we saw a ton of wildlife on our 4 hour evening safari. no lines to get in for the evening safaris so thats a plus and the sunset doesnt disappoint either. yes, theres lots of other jeeps around as well. yes, once theres elephants spotted there will be other jeeps around, especially at the bigger watering holes. we also got to see plenty of elephants and other wildlife with nobody else around as well along the drive. there are some leopards in the park, but we did not see any on our outing. id definitely recommend this to anyone interested in the wildlife of sri lanka. it was a super cool experience. we saw, elephants, crocodiles, buffalo, peacocks, tons of birds, monkeys, a few monitor lizards etc...

review_text_clean: we had a great morning on safari at udawalale national park. we got picked up from our homestay falcons nest at 5am and waited in the queue. lots of drivers like to go nice and early to get in quickly - the animals are better in the morning you usually see more. the sun rising as we travelled through the park was amazing. we saw so many elephants - one came so close that our guide had to reverse! we also saw crocodiles, water buffalo, wildcats, jeckalls, peacocks hundreds of them! and lots of other birds. unfortunately no leopards for us but as there are only approx 15 in the whole park, its very unusual to see them! we barely saw any other jeeps throughout our 3.5 hours in the park and were able to watch the elephants so peacefully with only one other jeep. highly recommend udawalale if youre wanting to see elephants booking through your hotelhomestay is the best option as they tend to have a guide they use. you can also visit the elephant transit home after and see the elephants being fed!
aspect_sentences: ['we had a great morning on safari at udawalale national park.']

review_text_clean: we spent this morning at udawalawa national park with lahiru as our guide. myself, husband and young daughter nearly 3, we had the jeep to ourselves. we saw more than we could have hoped, various types of birds, deer, mongoose, monkeys, crocodile, water buffalo and elephants up close. the best part was when we were by a small pond and waiting for a herd of elephant to come over, including 2 babies - we were the only ones there, it was very special. lahiru is very knowledgable and can spot all types of animals from far away, he knows the park very well which meant we were never close to other jeeps. hes also great at getting photos! it was very special , and our daughter loved it. it was perfectly safe for her. highly recommend lahiru. i organised our tour very easily through whatsapp 9476 272 6799

review_text_clean: after reading reviews on ta we decided to take a safari. we simply whatsapp lahiru, who has been mentioned many times he made all the arrangements. a driver picked us up from our villa, we switched into lahirus jeep at the entrance, did a 4 hour ride around then back home. it was quite a long day with lots of traveling. we found him very informative had a keen eye to spot thing we could never have seen. we seemed lucky in that we saw so many elephants all over the park, including 1 week old calves who could barely walk in a straight line without falling over. also plenty of birds, buffalo, lizards, a few crocodile, red spotted deer, monkeys giant squirrels. the tracks around were rutted in places but thats to be expected. the jeeps everybody seems to use are clearly up to job make for a great experience.
aspect_sentences: ['the jeeps everybody seems to use are clearly up to job make for a great experience.']

review_text_clean: we were staying at a fairly newly opened local hotel royal reach family resort 12hr drive from the national park and their lovely staff helped us organise this unforgettable 3 hour long safari in their hotel jeep. they also promised to get us an english speaking guide who turned out to be an absolute expert on all the wonderful creatures and plants! to be seen there. we picked him up at the entrance of the national park and with our guide on board our safari was off to a great start. lakshan is a volunteer guide and he turned out to be a real expert. he worked closely with the driver to take us away from the crowds into the heart of the park, spotting herd after herd of elephants, filling us with exciting facts and anecdotes about each animal encountered along the way peacocks perched on top of tall trees, gorgeous birds of all shapes and colours, lizards and buffaloes. lakshan has a very extensive knowledge of the fauna and flora of udawalawe park and he is a skilled educator, too, he taught us how to recognise different species, how to tell the age and sex of the elephants, his enthusiasm for this place was contagious. lakshan is also very patient so throughout the trip we had plenty of time to take fantastic pictures without being rushed. the three hours we spent with him exploring the national park were the highlight of our sri lankan trip. the whole safari for two people was about 60 including the jeep, entrance fees and a voluntary contribution to our guide! i cannot recommend him highly enough. if you would like to contact lakshan - you can find him on facebook lakshan geeganaarachchi he was the guide for prince edward- earl of essex and his wife when they visited udawalawe last year!. he is brilliant!
aspect_sentences: ['they also promised to get us an english speaking guide who turned out to be an absolute expert on all the wonderful creatures and plants!', 'we picked him up at the entrance of the national park and with our guide on board our safari was off to a great start.']

review_text_clean: our first safari experience and we really enjoyed it. i would say to make sure your guides are good as ours was awful, we got no information other than pointing to the animals and naming them- wow. dont know the name but booked through capital lanka bh lanka. but this didnt ruin the experience and seeing the elephants in the wild was wonderful. the first hour was quiet we maybe only saw 2-3 elephants, peacock and a land monitor. but when we went to the clearing by the lake there was 10s of elephants, birds, spotted deer, water buffalo, a crocodile in the distance, painted stork, and a mongoose. make sure you take water and suncream with you and maybe a snack too as a large part is of course waiting around to find the animals. most of the cars we saw are covered but depending on time of day the sun still comes through the sides. the timing was right for us at about 3 hours, we knew a day tour or several days wouldnt interest us so great taster and amazing to see these animals in the wild.

review_text_clean: entry fees skyrocketed about 2 weeks ago. solo travelers pay 43usd, which is about 7usd more than two travelers entering together and so on 43usd for individuals vs 36 usd if youre a couple. also, as a point of reference the current entrance fee for kruger national park in south africa is 27usd. 43usd is an extremely high entrance fee for any national park in the world. i know theres a cost savings on vehicles when you share one, but a solo traveler penalty is ridiculous. i tried to find people at the gate entrance to share a safari with. many of the tourists were interested, but the guides have a mafia type wilderness association and refused to let any tourists share costs. was it worth it? maybe once. well, when others described herds of elephants in their reviews, i was expecting herds, like in tanzania, kenya or like other places in africa. i believe herds in sri lanka means families of elephants, which numerically speaking are smaller-- maybe 5 or 6 in a family vs 10 in africa. there is a good variety of wildlife-- elephants, deer, monkeys, buffalo, crocodiles, mongoose, jackals, boar, peacocks and other birds. it was nice. if youre interested in going, i eventually went with the owner of my homstay, nalaka, 94 77 635 8192. he took me on a 4 hour jeep safari for 8,500 rp. he was great at spotting birds baby elephants, and other wildlife that other guides who denied me didnt see.
aspect_sentences: ['he was great at spotting birds baby elephants, and other wildlife that other guides who denied me didnt see.']

review_text_clean: we had an incredible time in udawalawe in large part because we booked with the incredible mansala safari resort. whether staying in their beautiful hotel or just taking their safari, we cant recommend them enough theyre one of the best choices ive made while travelling. mansala basically arrange everything safari, binoculars, transit, entry to the national park and you pay at the end. it was one of the cheapest options we found but also one of the best. tirons guide tharanga took us on our safari. like tiron, hes locally born and a genuine animal lover. he did everything the guidebooks tell you youll want in a guide he was respectful of the animals, never crowded them, avoided hotspots full of other drivers, gave us information without overloading us, and showed us everything. we saw - a herd of baby elephants - crocodiles - water buffalo - lots of deer, including stags and, essentially, bambi - a family of wild boar, including 8 gorgeous little piglets running about in what my partner called the best thing ive ever seen - lots of birds, including peacocks, storks, different types of eagles, woodsand pipers, little green bee eaters really beautiful, cormorants, lapwings, hoopoes - a surprise tortoise - surprise mongeese you can do an evening or morning safari, or both. we did an evening safari, which finishes before 6pm we arrived at 2pm and went straight out onto it, which was more than enough time. the hotel itself is a lovely family-run operation, with two rooms and the family living in the building. despite the homey, personal feel, everything from the food to the rooms to the safari is of the highest possible standard. food is cooked by the family, eaten on the veranda with animals around and is some of the best we ate on our trip. eat there rather than going out into udawalawe. the room was one of the best we stayed in in sri lanka, despite often paying significantly more than at mansala beautiful, comfortable, well-equipped, modern everything we needed. tiron, who runs the place, is a really kind and generous man. he was born in the house youre staying in, knows the local area really well, and was one of our favourite people we met in sri lanka. when the driver hed booked for our 2-hour drive to mirissa was suddenly unavailable, he took us himself. his number is 94 77 795 9090 - review_text_clean: we took a 3 hr safari booked through viator with bentota travel. bentota travel is another story so im not going to say anything about that. we arrived at the reserve after going to the elephant sanctuary and transferred to a jeep. access to the jeep required climbing in through a narrow gap at the back of the vehicle while standing on a beer crate!!! not easy for a couple of portly nearly 60 year olds, but it makes for a good story afterwards!! we engaged the services of a guide they do not charge as such, you just tip them at the end of the safari what you think their services were worth i would thoroughly recommend getting a guide. we didnt know where to look and the driver is too busy keeping his eye on the track to spot for you. in the end it was so worth having him as he was able to point out monitors, lizards, and birds that we just wouldnt have spotted. we saw wild buffalo, jackals, numerous colourful birds and birds of prey, turtles, lizards, monitors and loads of elephants. we were lucky enough to see a family group of about 10 elephants along with 2 week old calf, a couple of smaller family groups, numerous single elephants including one asleep leaning against a tree!, but the highlight was a mother and calf pair who crossed the track in front of us and went to the lake edge to drink. they then proceeded to bathe and play in the water. at the same time, they were surrounded by buffalo complete with storks standing on their backs i kid you not!! all in all, an amazing 3 hrs and some of it quite emotional. we didnt seem to drive for more than a couple of minutes without seeing something. we did however meet some landrovers with tourists and guide who had been in the park for 2 hrs and hadnt seen anything more than a couple of birds. i think we were extremely lucky and we happened to drop on a good guide who knew his stuff. amazing experience. p.s. getting out of the jeep was much easier, i went out through the front drivers window!!!!
aspect_sentences: ['we engaged the services of a guide they do not charge as such, you just tip them at the end of the safari what you think their services were worth i would thoroughly recommend getting a guide.']

review_text_clean: i booked myself partner in for an 8 hour tour of udawalawe which we visited today, we choose lahiru prasad as our guide on a friends recommendation ta reviews booked him via whatsapp 94 76 272 6799. the national park itself has amazing scenery, lagoons, bush jungle along with lots of wildlife. we saw many different bird species including hawk, horn bills, fish owl, hummingbird, bee-eaters jungle fowl, along with crocodiles, spotted deer, chameleons, mongoose, monitor lizards, wild boar and a pack of the rarely spotted golden jackal! we also saw 30 elephants, solo males herds of females along with 2 babies, one of which was only 2 months old. most of our elephant spottings were just us alone with no other jeeps around, we were able to sit with a herd of females baby eating grass around the jeep for over half an hour! without sounding like an advert this was 100 down to lahiru, he knows the park very well took us on different trails to find the animals that other jeeps werent on. hes super knowledgeable about all the animals answered any questions we had managed to spot animals other jeeps with just a driver were driving past missing. as it is also mating season the male elephants were quite difficult to approach, despite this we felt very safe confident in lahirus jeep. over the 8 hours lahiru was still stopping showing us things until we left the park, being so close to the elephants was an unforgettable experience, thank you lahiru driver udawalawe national park! lahiru also took us for a proper local curry afterwards organised a very well priced taxi on to ella for us!

review_text_clean: set off from hotel at 6am just as dawn was breaking. fabulous view of trees against lightening sky. couldnt get a pic tho as driver going too fast. arrived at the park with what seemed like a lot of people. but dubious at first we were going to be in one long traffic jam but the groups soon separated and we had the place to ourselves- mainly. saw elephants very close up, lots of birds including eagles, water buffalo, deer, monkeys and a crocodiles nose ??. the ride was bumpy but we felt safe. the drivers are excellent at spotting things to see and are very patient. the best bit for me - sorry all you animal lovers - was a lake we stopped at. gorgeous view of trees silhouetted across the lake. some beautiful trees in the park too. very worth the time and effort imo. beautiful place - very unspoiled.

review_text_clean: we loved our udawalawe national park safari experience, from arriving at dusk and seeing the elephants waiting for bananas along the fence line, to the hospitability and great food at mansala safari house and, of course, our animal packed private sunrise safari tour it was a magical 24 hours and one of the highlights of the trip! we booked only a few days before and were able to arrange a private safari through tiron from mansala safari house, all through whatsapp and for a very reasonable price. on the day we were greeted by a lovely driver who spoke great english. there was no need to get a guide as he had a keen eye and was very good at spotting animals. he also provided us with binoculars! when we entered the park entrance, there were probably 50 or so other jeeps but once we were let in we found that we were mostly alone during our 4 hour safari. if you are worried you will be in a line of jeeps and wont see any animals we totally recommend you book with tiron and stay at the mansala safari house.

review_text_clean: due to our visit in sri lanka this safari was on our list so we couldnt wait to feel the amazing experience being in nature, in the heart of a jungle where wild life exists and live. after having spend around 2 hours and a half driving from hikkaduwa and made a short stop to elephant transit home to see the orphan elephants we took the special jeep for the safari. the day was perfect for such an activity warm but not hot and partly cloudy. our driver was very good and was able to found all the hidden animals around the area, also very well educated regarding the animals and their bahviour. we had so great time as we met a lot elephants alone or families, bulls, snake, peacocks, many birds and some crocodile and all in very close distance, like being part of this place. we met the youngest elephant of the safari which was 4 months old next to his mother and the oldest which was 45 years old. a great experience that we strongly recommend to all tourists that is going to visit sri lanka. also is not a so expensive tour. we had this tour with norlanka tours which are very good and very well organised company.

review_text_clean: we enjoyed our afternoon jeep safari with lahiru on the 17th in some fabulous weather. the safari jeep had six seats which we had all for ourselves - a group of 2 adults and 2 children. lahiru had some water and snacks for us and he took us on off-beaten paths with no other jeeps around. out in the park we saw eagles, bee-eaters, jackals, turtles, a croc, storks, pelicans, spotted deer, a hornbill, a magnificent brown fish owl, monitor lizards, kingfishers, cormorants, the ubiquitous peacocks and at least five herds of elephants spread across different locations totalling around fifty in all, some with one-month old babies. that i guess was pretty much everything one could spot in the park. lahiru made us spend about twenty minutes close to a herd with baby elephants. it was exhilarating to see these mighty beasts in their eye, so close up. lahirus photography skills were excellent too! the drive back past the udawalawe reservoir in fading light was also awesome. i would say, this was well worth the 150 for 4-hours of absolute bliss - we must have covered at least 40kms in all. we had chosen lahiru based on the glowing ta reviews and boy, he did not disappoint. contacting him at 94 762726799 was a breeze. one piece of advice- those with sensitive airways could do well with some masks because of the trailing dust from a jeep ahead of you on those dry jungle tracks.

review_text_clean: this park really needs to change the way they do safaris and limit the amount of vehicles in the park. the problem is that they allow hotels to arrange safaris--which all compete with each, this results in an abundance of vehicles in the park with only 1-2 people. so when you see a family of elephants, too many vehicles swarm around them, prohibiting the animals from moving in the direction they want, and causing them to be stressed. furthermore, with so many vehicles in one area, the exhaust smell is strong and the engines are loud---also not good for the elephants. the park also needs to be stricter with the drivers by reminding them to keep distance and respect the animals. we all found this experience to be very troubling. i highly suggest when you book your safari, try booking through the park itself, and ask to be put with others in vehicles to limit them in the park. these animals need to be respected in their living space.

review_text_clean: we had a fantastic half-day safari where we spotted elephants, buffalo, deer, crocodiles, and a gazillion peacocks and other cool birds. we booked through our hotel and had an excellent guide who was very knowledgeable and could spot a green parrot in a tree from 20 metres! from reading other reviews it seems like you get what you pay for. when we were queuing we were worried about all the other vehicles around us but when we got into the park everyone went their separate ways. maybe we were lucky, however - corona virus and the time of year meaning fewer tourists than usual. also, i imagine some of the roads we drove down would be impassable in the wet season, forcing all the jeeps onto a few larger roads. all in all, i loved it and got the chance to see elephants in the wild.

review_text_clean: this was more like harassing elephants than spotting them in an eco friendly way. imagine at least 20 vehicles converging on a herd of elephants another 20 on their way. it was like a circus. the jeep i went with could have taken another couple but instead they put them in a jeep of their own there were plenty of others with sole occupants. this highlighted that it was a more a money making initiative for each driver than for the mental well being of the elephants. i have more vehicles in my photos than elephants. it is not something i will ever do again ever. the poor elephants having to put up with all that in your face stuff, with some being quite distressed due to a constant stream of vehicles blocking their paths. it left me feeling appalled that i even did it. it was wrong on a number of fronts. firstly their is the mental health of the poor elephants to consider, then of course you have all those vehicles car pooling is not considered, ripping up the environment, fuel consumption exhaust contributing to the greenhouse gas emissions, should i go on. so it definitely was not environmentally friendly in so many ways. if you are considering going then consider the above.

review_text_clean: we had a brilliant safari this morning with lahiru at udawalawe national park. we were picked up from our hotel in ella at 4.30 by lahirus driver and taken to udawalawe. from there we jumped in the land rover and started the safari. within a few minutes we saw some elephants not too far from the side of the road, then within another few minutes we saw a single male elephant right next to the road. we couldnt believe it! lahiru was keen to make sure we saw as much as we could and had plenty of time to get photographs. he pointed out everything he saw including chameleons hiding on branches. his driver turned the engine off when we got near any animals so we could take our time to photograph them or just stare in amazement. apart from on the main toad we only saw other safari vehicles twice. the vehicle we went in was a land rover which meant we could go off the main roads people usually take and went down to the lake, lots of the other vehicles cant do this because of the wet ground. towards the end of our safari we came across some more elephants, we stopped briefly and headed past them to a lake to see the crocodiles before the sun got too hot. then we went back to where the elephants were and just patiently sat while they got nearer to us, and we realised they had a baby with them. it was the most amazing thing, just being able to sit and watch them and being so close to them. we would highly recommend lahiru to anyone thinking about doing a safari. other animals we saw include water buffaloes, land monitors, deer, jackels, lots of birds including king fishers, crested eagle and loads of peacocks. after our safari the driver took us onwards to mirissa. doing a day trip was perfect and it was brilliant that we were picked up and dropped off so we didnt need to worry about transport. if youve not got much time in sri lanka dont miss this day trip! just drop him a whatsapp message 94 76 272 6799. thanks again - adam amber

review_text_clean: we visited the park on an evening safari beginning at 2pm and finishing at 5pm. i highly recommend making sure you are there as late or as early as possible as a number of animals came out towards the end of the tour as it cooled down. tour was great and the driver was very experienced and was able to show us a number of different animals long before we could see anything wild cat, lizards, monkeys, birds, bambi and as expected plenty of elephants. it was definitely worth the trip. only four stars though because these tours have a long way to go to meet the price they charge. all the vehicles follow each other in the park and you almost go up the same route you came down, and only experience a small part of the park. if they were to replicate the safaris in africa i have been lucky enough to experience they would benefit from two way radios in the car so they can communicate when they see something, a guide to provide info on the history and about the animals and sealed roads to cover larger areas where is the money going from all these tours??. this would allow them to cover more of the park and enhance the experience for the consumer.

review_text_clean: my wife and i went on an afternoon safari with chaminda, we were very specific that we wanted a quieter tour not harassing animals etc and staying away from the other jeeps where possible. chaminda to his credit was very professional and careful in his driving and approach of the animals and birds that i think we saw much more than other jeeps that seemed to be racing around. our guide was very informative, spotting the following blue tailed bee eater malabar pied hornbill peahens and peacocks brown headed barbet mongoose little green bee eater white bellied sea eagle changeable hawk eagle coppersmith barbet red vented bulbul green pigeon imperial pigeon sri lanka green pigeon sirkeer malkoha crested serpent eagle rose ringed parakeets brown shrike indian blue robyn water buffalos wallowing in a pond and of course elephants, some with very young calves. the highlight of our tour was the pied hornbills as i believe these are shy birds so rare sighting. overall a very enjoyable and informative tour. i can highly recommend chaminda, give him a ring or text phone no 94773379470. cheers michael and asha, from darwin australia.

review_text_clean: a must do experience wherever you are in sri lanka...we used a reputable courier to book the jeep hire and park fees which cost approximately 70. pay the bit extra for the more expensive jeep which is more substantially equipped than the cheaper model...believe me, youll be glad of it on the parks trails, which are very very unstable! our guide was very informative and pointed out things we would have easily missed, they are incredibly professional and well informed, not to mention exceptional drivers! within minutes we were in the company of a majestic bull elephant who seemed quite undeterred by our proximity! we booked a couple of hours in the park, enough time to get up close and personal with the famous residents, including deer, water buffalo and a vast array of birds, lizards and mongoose, perhaps a longer tour might have increased our chances of seeing more than the 5 or 6 elephant we did, but by then wed been bounced around enough! this is well worth the fee and advisable early start, if just to be that close to these magnificent creatures.

review_text_clean: i had the most fantastic day with chaminda, and recommend him wholeheartedly. he is polite, professional, sensitive to travellers needs and speaks pretty good english. he knows the names of all the animals in english and has reference books in the jeep. most importantly he is knowledgeable about the creatures in the park and has a very good eye for spotting all manner of birds, mammals, and lizards. you can call him directly on his mobile 94 077 337 9470 chaminda charged me the standard rate for each half day game drive currently 5,000 rupees and freely gave me extra time on the morning drive in order to arrive early and beat the long queues, and then added more free extra time at the end too, as he was trying to find a brown fish owl. he spotted so many rare birds for me, and the brown fish owl eluded us on this trip! the afternoons are best for elephants as its too hot for birds until late afternoon, when visitors have to exit the park. here are some of the notable sightings we had over the day brown shrike yellow eyed babbler rare woolly neck stork blue faced malkohas rare sirkeer malkohas rare red breasted green pigeon indian roller jungle prinia sikri great coucal grey headed fish eagle kingfisher common and black capped chestnut headed bee eater little green bee eater blue tailed bee eater land monitor lizard painted storks plum headed parakeet pair rare hoopoe crocodiles serpent eagle sri lankan green pigeon tufted grey langur toque macaques mogoose pair yellow water lapwing golden jackal plus common many elephants including little babies, lots of fascinating behaviours to observe peacocks water buffaloes egrets brahminy kites

review_text_clean: i didnt really want to book a tour with lahiru because it seems like everyones reviews are about him and his prices keep going up. but we really had a great experience with lahiru!! i would highly recommend him. we saw elephants up so close but really felt like lahiru respected the animals. we didnt see huge amounts of elephants but saw approx 5 different groups along with water buffalo, crocodiles !, lizards and 15 different birds. lahirus ability to spot wildlife can only come from years of experience. whenever we came across another jeep, lahiru went another way so we had a truly private tour the whole 4 hours. we had heard about lahiru taking photos through his binoculars and i hadnt thought much of it. but lahiru was so skilled at taking photos with your own phonecamera that you could just focus of looking at the wildlife rather than trying to take a good photo. lahiru arranged pick up from ella and then we were dropped off at a beach in the south after the tour. he even organised an extra driver from ella in the morning because a land slide had blocked a road and the extra driver could navigate a different route. the whole day cost 250 usd for three people. we booked via whatsapp 94762726799. lahiru also brought food for us but we didnt know that was going to happen so we had brought our own!. only feedback for lahiru tell people you will bring them food, give them more information before the day or when you meet them so they know how the day will run we knew when we were being picked up and approx how long the tour went for, but when we met lahiru it was literally just a warm hello and then we didnt know what was happening next - i guess it was just a case of lets get on with the safari but we werent sure what was going on, and let the people know when the tour is coming to an end this wasnt clear and we were told we could choose how long we wanted to stay in the park. the time went so fast!

review_text_clean: we booked our safari through mansala safari house and went for the full day option. at the park entrance, we were greeted by lionel, one of the volunteer guides note that this is an additional cost and we are very happy to have had him with us - he has eagle eyes, quite literally, as he pointed out eagles and other wild birds we would otherwise have missed, and even spotted small lizards high up in trees and a tiny musk deer deep in the undergrowth. elephants, of course, are easier to spot and we met plenty along the way. our driver and guide were both fairly respectful of their space, and although all the vehicles in the park are quite noisy, the wildlife in general seemed relatively undisturbed. in the afternoon, we were incredibly excited to see a leopard and as there were no other jeeps around, we stood for 5 to 10 minutes observing him. something i think well never forget! our guide and driver were almost as excited as we were by this rare sighting. it was clearly our lucky day, as we later came across a jungle cat. id heartily recommend a visit to the udawalawe national park and if you stay at the mansala safari house, they send you off with the most delicious lunch, even catering for vegans like us! total cost for two people in one jeep, with driver, was usd 130 23,400 lkr. lionels services were additional, with a voluntary and discretionary contribution.
aspect_sentences: ['id heartily recommend a visit to the udawalawe national park and if you stay at the mansala safari house, they send you off with the most delicious lunch, even catering for vegans like us!']

review_text_clean: we went in the afternoon slot around 3.30 p.m but unfortunately didnt see a lot of animals other than elephants. it also started raining heavily about an hour after we entered so we had to cover the vehicle, reducing our visibility. while we saw lots and lots of elephants, we werent lucky enough to see the other animals that other reviewers have seen. to be honest though, the elephants themselves were completely worth the money and my children had a wonderful time. a couple of tips - if you get quotes from a few guys and go asking further down the road, you will invariably get a cheaper rate. however you will spend time doing this, which means that you might save 1 or 2 thousand lkr but lose out on safari time, so the savings arent really worth it. my recommendation is to plan ahead, check with a few operators and book a safari the previous day. try to go early and reschedule if heavy rains are predicted. just for information - the pricing model is like this the operator will either offer an all-in rate inclusive of jeep and entrance tickets or will offer his jeep for a certain price and ask you to buy tickets on your own you need to specifically ask for the second option. the price of the jeep will be approximately lkr 6000 for 3 hours, which you can try and negotiate. the price is for the whole jeep 6 seater, regardless of the number of people, so you can team up with other guests at your hotel and reduce the per-person cost.

review_text_clean: the orphanage itself was amazing and we didnt see any elephants being harmed however, the workers at the elephant orphanage were rude and are only there to make tips off you. at first, they are very helpful wanting to take your photo and show us more elephants but then took us to a remote part of the orphanage were no other guests could see us and asked for a tip. my partner gave them a tip of nearly 1000 after already tipping another staff member 1000 and 500 and bought fruits for feeding the elephants with came to 1500 this is after paying a 15 entrance per person. when they took us to do remote parts of the orphanage, which was behind a building away from other guests and cameras they asked for a higher tip whilst one of the staff members were sharpening his massive knife. this obviously made us feel very uncomfortable and we ended up leaving the orphanage look out area after being there only 10 minutes. if you was to go, i would suggest that you go and watch the elephants down at elephant bay hotel and dont enter the zoo its self. saying this we did have a lovely time and got some really lovely photos but just felt very unsettled by the whole experience.

review_text_clean: i had visited this place in 2007 and saw maimed elephants herehurt by landmines during the civil strife. this time around the elephants looked healthy. i went to see the elephants taking a bath in the ma oya river. some frolicked while two were held down in the waters so that visitors could touch them and sit on them for a photo opportunity. the mahouts would not let the elephants stand up if they wanted to. for an orphanage that claims to be the worlds largest, this certainly is not nice to watch. would i recommend visitors to go there? i am an eternal optimist. if the fees paid by visitors to watch the elephants can in any way improve the treatment meted out to them, it should be encouraged.

review_text_clean: the elephant sanctuary in sri lankas pinnawala town is a major sanctuary for orphaned and injured elephants. the road to the orphanage is perhaps one of the most scenic drive you may come across in sri lanka. the star attraction of the sanctuary was an elephant which has given birth to twins, a rarity. we were also able to see a few elephants in search of a mate. away from the orphanage across the road the elephants were given a cool bath in the river. there are also a number of souvenir shops near the elephant bathing ghat. the parking space is spacious and the western style toilets were clean and well maintained. there is also an atm near the entrance where the newly arrived foreign tourists can convert their home currency into sri lankan rupees. a fun place for kids to see elephants of all ages at close proximity. the entry fee is nominal and the place well maintained. we could not locate a restaurant in the premises. we could also see a number of birds in the surroundings. a good place to visit with the kids for a picnic. recommended.
aspect_sentences: ['we could not locate a restaurant in the premises.']

review_text_clean: a bit of a mixed review. i do agree with lots of the reviews here, its not an elephant orphanage, its a tourist attraction. its clear the elephants are trained , some of them are chained to rocks in order to tame them around people, we did see some not so nice treatment of elephants, which at times was uncomfortable. on the flip side to this, as someone who has never been close to elephants before it was amazing to see so many in the river playing. it was definitely an experience and to be honest i dont regret going but im not 100 sure if i would go again just because of the animal treatment. also be aware - this is 100 a money making tourist attraction. we stayed in the hotel right on the water thats another review in itself.. but when we arrived if we wanted to go to our hotel we had to pay an entry fee to the park then if you want a photo or to touch or feed the elephants, its made out this is fine but youre then demanded to pay the staff , and they want more than you give them. a tough one to review, as a brit it did seem a little odd and hard to tell what treatment the animals get, but it was an experience we wont forget - so i think you have to make your mind up based on the reviews.

review_text_clean: we landed in colombo around 7.30am and headed straight up to the pinnawala elephant orphanage which was around 2.53 hour drive. be sure to time your visit when the elephants do their walk from the park down to the river, which happens twice a day, this is an amazing sight seeing a herd of elephants bathing and wandering around in the river area. as close to them being in the wild and their natural habitat as you can get. this experience alone is well worth the visit, the rest of the park is average with elephants grazing in different areas. one highlight was seeing the twin baby elephants with their mother. there are a few informational boards scattered around the park but apart from this information was lacking. wear a hat and cover yourself in sunblock, take water, as there is nowhere to escape the sun. be aware of people trying to sell you fruits to feed the elephants on their walk which is frowned upon and of course they can be quite persistent. maximum two hours is all you will need here.
aspect_sentences: ['as close to them being in the wild and their natural habitat as you can get.']

review_text_clean: let me start by saying i have visited the pinnewala elephant orphanage many times dating back to 1985. the spirit of the place has certainly changed and unfortunately i now cannot recommend this place to ethically or fair-minded tourists. i wont comment on the treatment of the animals - there is a lot of info in other reviews about this. my main issue is the price - it costs approximately 16.50 for a foreigners ticket. bearing in mind that this is approximately what you would pay for an adults entry to a large, well-kept urban zoo with adequate facilities in europe or the united states, the experience falls far short of that. there are far better ways to see elephants in sri lanka than to support this racket. give it a miss and go to one of the national parks instead if you can.

review_text_clean: as a volunteer at an elephant hospital in thailand i was very sceptical of coming here and looked at previous reviews. but in my experience this is one of the better lives that elephants can be offered in todays world. the way the park is planned with the rotation of the elephants some bathing, some eating fruit, some in the free land, was planned with the elephants in mind. the control measures are there but not over the top and it is one of the better places for elephants to be that can no longer be integrated into the wild. im not sure how far orphanage has been stretched, but if you take it for what it is, they do a good job to sustain this business so that the elephants can live, when it is not feasible for them to be in the wild.

review_text_clean: we ventured to this orphanage on a ships shore ex ... its about a 2 - 2.5 hour drive from the port on a coach. i think if you can get here with a local guide you would be better off as you can spend as much or as little time as you like at the orphanage, whereas on a ships tour the time is shorter. this orphanage is a government run orphanage and at least paying guests are aware of this when they enter and hopefully all money raised goes towards the elephants upkeep and setting them free back into the jungle. i found all the public areas where we went and the enclosures we saw were very clean and tidy. take sri lankan money with you - although you can use cc at the orphanage shop and other shops in the town, generally speaking they dont take cash unless its sri lankan money. there is an opportunity to feed the elephants by hand in one areas of the orphanage however rupees are required - no usd or other currency and definitely no cc there !! luckily our guide exchanged some usd for rupees but the fruit was gone very quickly. yes there were a few elephants chained up in another enclosure but of the three enclosures we saw, this was the only one where they were chained. the reason we were given for this was because they are wild animals... lets face it ... if they are males and are maturing, they could get annoyed about something and cause injuries to other elephants if not their handlers and or the public if they crashed through the fence. indeed at the elephant feeding area i saw one elephant get grumpy with another one for muscling in on the food i was feeding it - the elephant turned around and head butted the second elephant in its side to show its displeasure at eating its food. the third area where we saw elephants at this orphanage, the elephants were roaming free in a large treed area ... i wondered if this was the first stage of getting them used to fending for themselves before setting them free in the jungle. we had lunch included in our ships shore excursion at a hotel by the river and luckily for us, they had quite a few elephants bathing there - a lovely thing to see. imo, this excursion is not suitable for mobility impaired people because the terrain to get to the elephant enclosures is not paved and the surface is uneven. theres also a few steps to negotiate within the elephant orphanage area. also, the road to the hotel where we went for lunch was not paved either.

luckily our guide exchanged some usd for rupees but the fruit was gone very quickly. yes there were a few elephants chained up in another enclosure but of the three enclosures we saw, this was the only one where they were chained. the reason we were given for this was because they are wild animals... lets face it ... if they are males and are maturing, they could get annoyed about something and cause injuries to other elephants if not their handlers and or the public if they crashed through the fence. indeed at the elephant feeding area i saw one elephant get grumpy with another one for muscling in on the food i was feeding it - the elephant turned around and head butted the second elephant in its side to show its displeasure at eating its food. the third area where we saw elephants at this orphanage, the elephants were roaming free in a large treed area ... i wondered if this was the first stage of getting them used to fending for themselves before setting them free in the jungle. we had lunch included in our ships shore excursion at a hotel by the river and luckily for us, they had quite a few elephants bathing there - a lovely thing to see. imo, this excursion is not suitable for mobility impaired people because the terrain to get to the elephant enclosures is not paved and the surface is uneven. theres also a few steps to negotiate within the elephant orphanage area. also, the road to the hotel where we went for lunch was not paved either.
